neighbours.label: ' what' / ' Whatever' opening a free relative or a rhetorical 'what' clause ('Whatever your day looks like', 'share what surprised you')
fire: Whatever your weekend looks like, try to get some rest.
Please tell us what interested you most.
We played golf in a storm (what were we thinking?).
Whatever your budget is, there is a plan for you.
Share what you learned with the rest of the class.
They forgot the tent (what a mess that was).
Whatever the weather does, the fair will go on.
Ask them what worried them most about the move.
quiet: This weekend looks like a good one to get some rest.
Please tell us your name and address.
We played golf in a storm for an hour.
Your budget is fine, and there is a plan for you.
Share your notes with the rest of the class.
They forgot the tent at the old camp.
The weather is mild, and the fair will go on.
Ask them to carry the boxes during the move.
